headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Nullclaw’s filesystem/network-heavy CRM agent can ingest Haystack outputs and act on them without strong provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call REST APIs and MCP servers, and Nullclaw can read/write files, run browsers, and use MCP. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from Haystack can reach Nullclaw as instructions. The shared channel is documented, but no provenance or parser hardening is shown, so I rate this medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Haystack outputs are copied into Nullclaw via MCP, files, or webhook payloads
IF Nullclaw parses retrieved content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP bridging between the two agents
Route Haystack outputs through a plain-text sanitizer
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
Require human review before Nullclaw executes retrieved instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and MCP access, while Nullclaw touches sensitive classes including API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs. If shared workspace or message flow exposes those artifacts to Haystack, Haystack can exfiltrate them over the network. The pairwise leakage path is credible and the blast radius includes secrets, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Nullclaw workspace files or audit logs are exposed to Haystack through shared storage or MCP
IF Haystack forwards retrieved content to external APIs or web endpoints
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Block Haystack access to Nullclaw secret-bearing directories
Restrict Haystack egress to approved domains only
Rotate any secrets already present in shared files
Use redaction before any cross-agent file transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Haystack can also use MCP and broad network egress. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace or repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state. Because the profiles show overlapping write surfaces without locking, the conflict is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace path
IF either agent performs git commits or file writes without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace
Disable git writes for one agent during shared sessions
Add a file-locking wrapper around mutable paths
Serialize MCP tool calls through a single orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG agent that can surface retrieved content, and Nullclaw is a sales-CRM assistant with action-taking surfaces such as webhooks, browser use, subprocesses, and scheduling. If Nullclaw treats Haystack output as authoritative, retrieval errors can cascade into downstream actions. The action authority makes the blast radius high.
conditions: IF Haystack output is fed into Nullclaw without verification
IF Nullclaw uses that output to trigger webhooks, browser actions, or scheduled tasks
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Nullclaw acts on Haystack output
Require citations or source links for all retrieved claims
Limit Nullclaw to draft-only mode for cross-agent inputs
Log and review all downstream actions triggered from retrieval results

E_compliance.rationale: Nullclaw explicitly handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, service-account JSON, and audit logs, while Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics and has broad network egress. If regulated or secret-bearing data from Nullclaw is routed into Haystack, the pair can create a compliance breach through uncontrolled external transmission and retention. Haystack’s docs-only status means no residency or retention safeguards are evidenced.
conditions: IF secret-bearing or regulated data from Nullclaw is sent into Haystack
IF Haystack stores, logs, or forwards that data outside the intended residency boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Haystack inputs
Mask secrets before any transfer
Review retention and logging settings on both agents
Use a separate compliant system for secret-bearing workflows
